extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners; patent applicants and practitioners interacting with KIPO
extracted.subtask_description: Operational rules and substantive standards for Korean patent examination, reexamination, cancellation of measures, decisions to grant/reject, and handling of foreign-language applications. Focused on examiners' procedures and applicants' requirements in Korea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of written decision to grant a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The written decision to grant a patent shall include an application number, title of invention, name and address of applicant and agent, the text of the decision of patentability and its rationale, and number of claims to be patented, day/month/year of decision to grant a patent, matters having amended ex officio, along with an examiner's sign and seal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a decision to grant, the Commissioner of KIPO shall deliver a certified copy to the applicant; the decision is confirmed upon delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation requirement for special applicant classes before grant
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed by a KIPO patent examiner, by a KIPO examiner within 2 years of retirement, or by a searcher of a prior art search institution supervised by KIPO, if the patent examiner finds the examination should be registered based on results, the examiner shall determine allowance or refusal in consultation with 3 persons including a director of the examination division or head of the examination part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This consultation requirement applies prior to making the grant/refusal determination for those listed classes of applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and form of written decision to reject
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant fails to overcome notified grounds for rejection, the examiner shall make a written decision to reject an application with rationale attached; the written decision shall include application number, title of invention, name and address of applicant and agent, day/month/year of notice of grounds for rejection, the text of decision and its rationale, day/month/year of decision to reject, and examiner's sign and seal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a ground of rejection may be cured by ex‑officio amendment, the examiner shall make the ex‑officio amendment and allow grant (see matters subject to ex‑officio amendment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on introducing new rejection rationale at decision-to-reject stage
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall not make a decision to reject based on unreasonable rationale other than the already notified ground for rejection, which includes requesting new prior art documents without prior notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To refer to new prior art, the examiner must notify that fact as a ground for rejection (i.e., newly-found grounds must be separately notified).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling third-party information during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: When examining an application with information provided by a third party as grounds for rejection, an examiner shall take requisite measures before making the final decision and notify the information provider whether the provided information is used or not when the examination closes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if the information provider lacks capacity (incompetent/fictitious) or the application is abandoned/withdrawn/invalidated prior to examination, the examiner may not notify use of the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to legitimate right-holder when unentitled filing leads to rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner decides to reject an application based on the ground that it was filed by an unentitled person, the examiner shall deliver written notice to the legitimate right‑holder without delay after confirming the decision to reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If confirmation takes long due to appeals, the examiner may notify the legitimate right‑holder of the decision to reject and the existence of the appeal in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to consult on revoked-and-returned applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For patent applications which have been revoked and returned, the responsible examiner shall consult with a director of the examination division or head of the examination part and determine allowance or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation is required to resolve the appropriate final determination after remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of examination measures — conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may cancel a measure if the concerned measure displays definite defects and the benefits of its cancellation far outweigh the benefits of maintaining it; cancellation loses partial or whole validity retroactively to the very beginning and shall be made under the name of the examiner who originally conducted the measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation should be done only when law compliance benefits outweigh confidence protection; the examiner must review whether measures fall under cancellation in specified cases (resuming suspended/closed application, examining an application not requested for examination, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of measures — exceptions and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall not cancel notices of grounds for rejection, requests for amendment, or requests for supplementation because their cancellation is of less practical use compared to keeping them through amendment or error correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation of a measure carried out by an examiner shall be notified to the applicant with definite and specific explanation and reasons after communication to managing director; in principle, use the Patent Examination Processing System notice form, but On-nara EDMS may be used in specified situations (e.g., delays, new documents received, fee payment issues, system failures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to execute subsequent measures after cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: When cancelling a measure conducted by the examiner, the concerned examiner shall execute the corresponding subsequent measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation triggers the need to carry out corrective or follow-up procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to request reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days from receiving a certified copy of the decision to reject (or within an extended period if the appeal period is extended), the applicant may amend the specification or drawings to request reexamination of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination was introduced to reduce patent fee burden and complexity compared with previous pre-appeal reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination shall be assigned to the examiner who performed the original examination and decided to reject the application; however, if entrustment to the original examiner is inappropriate (e.g., transfer out of examination bureau), an examiner in charge of patent classification for the claimed invention shall carry out the reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment aims to maintain continuity but allows practical reassignment when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility requirements for requesting reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements: the application has not been invalidated, withdrawn or abandoned; has been rejected (excluding rejection after reexamination); has not requested an appeal trial against the decision to reject; and declares intention to request reexamination with amendment of the specification, drawings, or claims. 'Amendment' includes any amendment made in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request for reexamination is made by submission of the amendment; formalities for reexamination requests follow amendment examination procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities when reexamination request is defective
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reexamination request is filed for an application not pending (invalidated/withdrawn/abandoned), filed by a person other than applicant, or submitted after statutory period, the examiner shall provide the applicant an opportunity for explanation and return the written reexamination request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also return requests filed prior to decision to reject or repeated requests after a first reexamination rejection. If reexamination followed by remand leads to new grounds different from previous, applicant may request reexamination again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incompatibility of simultaneous appeal trial and reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant shall not request reexamination for an application for which an appeal trial against the decision to reject has been requested. When both are filed simultaneously, specific handling rules apply depending on the order/timing of amendment versus appeal notice (four scenarios described).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: if amendment submitted after notice of appeal, examiner returns the amendment but allows withdrawal of appeal to pursue reexamination within prescribed period; if appeal notice submitted after amendment, examiner treats reexamination as legitimate and proceeds; if both same day and submission order unclear, examiner will explain options and return amendment if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of reexamination request on previous decision to reject
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of a reexamination request, the previous decision to reject is deemed to have been withdrawn; the examiner shall examine as he/she would have before the decision to reject was made, though prior procedures (notices, amendments, refusals to enter amendment, etc.) remain valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reexamination only withdraws the decision to reject, not other prior procedural acts; scope of allowed amendments and refusal-to-enter standards follow prior amendment rules (see Article 47/Part VI Chapter 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of applicant confidence for pre-reexamination amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if an amendment made before the reexamination request would be refused to be entered later, the examiner shall not refuse to enter the amendment retroactively; this protects applicant confidence in relying on amendments made before reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is based on Article 51 proviso (amendment retroactively by the Proviso).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for judging introduction of new matter in reexamination amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: When judging whether an amendment introduces new matter under Article 47(2) or meets Article 47(3) amendment requirements, the comparison reference depends on prior treatment of earlier amendments: compare additions to the original specification/drawings for Article 47(2) and compare other amendment requirements to the specification/drawings as reflected by the last admitted amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two illustrative scenarios are given: (i) a sequence where Amendment I admitted then Amendment II admitted then Amendment III filed for reexamination — compare Addition vs. original; other requirements vs. the specification reflecting Amendment II; (ii) when Amendment III was previously refused entry, then for a later Amendment IV submitted with reexamination, do not consider refused Amendment III in the comparison for Article 47(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure after admission of amendment in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the amendment is regarded as appropriate, the examiner shall admit and reflect it in the specification to be examined; after confirming the specification, decide whether grounds for rejection remain and make the corresponding notice and decision to grant or reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amendment overcomes notified grounds but discloses other grounds not previously indicated, the examiner shall notify newly found grounds for rejection. If examiner issues non‑final/final rejection or decision to grant while disregarding partial inappropriateness, the amendment shall not be refused retroactively even if inappropriateness discovered later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure after refusal to enter amendment during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the amendment is refused entry, the examiner shall immediately proceed with the pre-amendment original specification; if grounds for rejection remain, make decision to reject; but if review finds the decision to reject improper and no other grounds, deliver decision to grant; if review finds other grounds, notify those grounds again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types of grounds for rejection to be referred from relevant chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination instructions on previously-notified grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the grounds for rejection previously notified are not overcome upon the reexamination request, those rejection grounds shall not be regarded as newly generated; the examiner shall admit the amendment but make a decision to reject the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if amendment fails to remedy other grounds than the ground on which the decision to reject was made, examiner shall provide an opportunity for submission of written arguments without immediately issuing a decision to reject, except where applicant had already had the opportunity and the ground was once overcome — then a decision to reject shall be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of filing a reexamination request on applicant actions
rubrics_metrics.description: When the request for reexamination is filed, the decision to reject is regarded as cancelled; therefore an applicant shall not perform acts which can be done within thirty days from receipt of the certified copy of the decision to reject such as filing a notice of appeal against the decision to reject or filing a divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, an applicant may file a divisional application either upon the request for a reexamination or within the period for submitting a written argument in response to a notice of grounds for rejection during the reexamination stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on withdrawal of reexamination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 67-2(3) stipulates that the request for a reexamination shall not be withdrawn to prevent procedural confusion; where an applicant submits a request for withdrawal, it is regarded as an uncertain document and the examiner shall provide opportunity for explanation and return the written request for withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This maintains procedural clarity since the decision to reject is deemed withdrawn when reexamination is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-language application — permitted languages and filing of Korean translation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant states the intention to prepare the specification and drawings in a language specified by Ordinance (English only as per Administrative Instructions), the specification and drawings may be written in that foreign language; the applicant shall submit a Korean translation of the specification and drawings by not later than one year and two months from the date specified in Article 64(1), or, upon receipt of a request for examination, within three months from the date notice is served or within one year and two months from earliest priority date, whichever is earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New Korean translations replacing earlier ones may be submitted within that time period except where the applicant has amended the specification or filed a request for examination; for divisional or converted applications filed in a foreign language, translations must be submitted within 30 days from filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and effect of Korean translations for foreign-language applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Korean translations shall be submitted accompanied by the document submission form and shall be 'word-for-word translation' into Korean in accordance with the context of the foreign-language specification. If Korean translations are submitted, the foreign-language specification shall be deemed amended according to the Korean translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Korean translations may be corrected for errors during the period set for amendments; corrections made before the last one are deemed not to have been made. New matter beyond original disclosure will be evaluated based on the Korean translations; mistranslations corrected allow amendment within scope of corrected translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to submit required Korean translations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Korean translations of a foreign-language specification are not submitted within the prescribed period, the patent application shall be deemed to have been voluntarily withdrawn. Failure to submit Korean translations of drawing text does not cause withdrawal but may give rise to amendment instructions for violation of written description requirement of drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only after Korean translations are submitted may the applicant file a request for examination, amend the specification, file divisional/converted applications or request early publication; patent rights and public inspection are based on the Korean specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of new matter in foreign-language applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination for a foreign patent application is basically the same as for regular applications; however, amendment to a specification/drawings originally attached to the foreign-language application or amendment based on the Korean translation has limits due to the characteristics of foreign-language applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New matter introduced via translation or subsequent amendment will be scrutinized with respect to original disclosure and translation-correction rules; see the specific limits and procedures in the chapter.
